item.title: SCP-5978
item.content:encoded:
Author, did you happen to follow the feedback-seeking process noted in the How to Write an SCP Guide? There are a lot of immediately noticeable errors, most of which could have been quickly fixed if noted before a mainsite post. For example:

SCP-5978 is a hourglass, standing 9.5 inches tall and has a 6-inch base.

  • Since "hourglass" starts with a vowel sound ("our-glass"), the article used should be "an" and not "a".
  • The Foundation is a scientific organization, and uses metric measurements. Inches are not metric measurements.
  • The parallel structure of "standing […] tall" and "has […] base" is inconsistent.
  • It's not certain what measurement for the base is. Presuming it's got a circular base, the measurement would be specified to the diameter rather than the length of a side.

The rest of the article is similarly in need of edits to maintain the clinical tone that a professional researcher would use. If you haven't looked at the feedback process yet, I highly recommend doing so if you want to submit a successful page to the mainsite.

item.title: SCP-5279
item.content:encoded:
This needs expansion. Why is it a coca-cola brand ball? Why does it kill you? It just doesn't really work, in my opinion.

A few things:

testing shows it’s resistant to fire, gunfire, blunt force, high calibre explosions, and even being doused in lava

Why would they test these things? When they discovered it, they would have realised it was indestructible, and it seems like it would be a waste of resources to just hit it with everything they have to destroy it. Just because something is indestructible doesnt mean that that fact needs to be tested, especially as foundation policy is to keep anomalies around.

it will start flashing the colors of the rainbow once something black, green, or shiny enters 2 feet within the radius of SCP-5279-2 or SCP-5279-1

If it goes within 2 feet1 of itself, it activates? Because it is SCP-5279-2.

In general, this article has no narrative, and even an anomaly that's interesting on its own doesnt really work without that. So … -1.

Footnotes
1. By the way, that needs to be in metric, as the foundation uses UN standard units
